MASTER.title: Master Legal Index
MASTER.subtitle: Missouri and federal rules, statutes, claim elements, landmark cases, deadlines and terms for a pro se litigant. Built as a first edition; sections marked "check subsection" need the exact subdivision confirmed against the current text.
MASTER.banner: Legal information, not legal advice. Rule numbers, statute sections, case citations and deadlines here are a working index. Confirm each against the official current text (Missouri Supreme Court Rules, Revised Statutes of Missouri, U.S. Code, Federal Rules, and the court’s local rules) before you rely on it or file it.
MASTER.placeholder: Search rules, statutes, cases, terms (e.g. 55.25, default, Monell)
MASTER.footer: First edition, compiled 2026-09-29. Companion volume: Garner Case Index. Volume II ties this reference to each pending matter.

sections.title: How to Use This Book
paras: Start in the Element Finder when you know the claim. Start in the rule blocks when you have a deadline. Start in Case Law when you need authority for a motion or a brief.
Filter by Missouri or Federal at the top. Many matters cross both systems, so the default is both.
Each entry flagged "check subsection" needs the exact subdivision confirmed. Rule numbers change; the official text controls.
Volume II, the Garner Case Index, maps every pending matter to the entries here.

sections.title: Standing Goal and Research Standard
paras: Goal: precise precision and the best result in each court case. Everything in this volume is held to that standard.
Source order: official current text in force on the relevant date, then annotated statutes, then verified opinion text, then secondary sources. Case-file notes are leads, never authority.
Citator standard: confirm that each case exists, the quote, the pin cite, the parallel cite, and its later history and treatment. Say so whenever only existence and cited-by counts could be checked.
Form standard: start from the court’s own forms, Missouri Approved Instructions, federal AO forms and local-rule formatting, and list every deviation.
Also check: local rules, rule and session-law effective dates, weekend and holiday roll-over, and consistency between matters.

sections.title: Claim and Defense Element Finder
sections.intro: Elements as generally stated in Missouri and federal law. Use these as a checklist, then pull the controlling case and the Missouri Approved Instructions (MAI) for the exact form.

items.d: (1) plaintiff owned or had the right to possess the property; (2) defendant took possession with intent to exercise control inconsistent with the owner’s rights; (3) owner deprived of the right to possess. Demand and refusal may be needed when possession was initially lawful.
Duty, breach, causation, damages.
Delivery of personal property for a purpose, acceptance, understanding that it be returned or disposed of as directed. Failure to return or wrongful release can support conversion or breach.

Representation; falsity; materiality; speaker’s knowledge of falsity; intent that it be acted on; hearer’s ignorance of falsity; reliance; right to rely; proximate injury. Plead with particularity (Rule 55.15).

Two or more persons; an unlawful objective or lawful objective by unlawful means; meeting of the minds; an overt act (tort) in furtherance; damages. Conspiracy is not a standalone tort without an underlying wrong.
Benefit conferred by plaintiff; defendant appreciated it; defendant accepted and retained it under circumstances that make retention unjust.

Purchase or lease of merchandise primarily for personal, family or household purposes; unlawful practice under § 407.020; ascertainable loss of money or property as a result. No purchase from the defendant is a common problem.

Publication; of a defamatory statement; that identifies the plaintiff; false; made with the required fault; damage to reputation. Statements to police may carry a qualified privilege defeated by malice or falsity known to the speaker.
Detention or restraint against the person’s will; without legal justification. Two-year limitation under § 516.140.
Earlier proceeding commenced against plaintiff; instigated by defendant; terminated in plaintiff’s favor; no probable cause; malice; damages.
Intentional intrusion into a private matter or place where the plaintiff has a reasonable expectation of privacy, highly offensive to a reasonable person.
Person acting under color of state law; seizure without probable cause (or without reasonable suspicion for a stop). Qualified immunity is the main defense.
Constitutional violation caused by an official policy, widespread custom, or decision of a final policymaker. No respondeat superior.
Disability; qualified for the job with or without accommodation; adverse action because of the disability. Timely EEOC charge is a prerequisite.
Eligible employee; covered employer; entitled to leave; gave notice; employer denied or interfered with benefits.
Protected activity; adverse action; causal connection.
Protected class or disability; adverse action; the protected trait was a contributing factor (Missouri standard is more plaintiff-friendly than the federal one). Charge to MCHR within 180 days.

items.k: Order of protection: sufficiency of evidence
items.d: Petitioner proves abuse or stalking by a preponderance of the evidence; appellate review under Murphy v. Carron.
